description: The chart titled 'Market share of Tesla vehicles by region (TTM)' is a line chart showing market share percentages over time from Q1 2017 to Q1 2023. The legend includes three series: US/Canada (blue line), Europe (red line), and China (green line). The Y-axis ranges from 0% to 4%, and the X-axis shows quarterly intervals. By Q1 2023, the US/Canada market share is approximately 3.8%, Europe is approximately 2.3%, and China is approximately 2%. The main trend shows a consistent growth in market share for Tesla across all three regions over the 6-year period, with the US/Canada region leading throughout and showing the most significant acceleration since 2021.

The chart 'Cumulative miles driven with FSD Beta (millions)' is a line graph showing growth from March 2021 to March 2023. The x-axis plots months from Mar-21 to Mar-23, and the y-axis shows cumulative miles in millions, ranging from 0 to 140. The graph shows an accelerating exponential trend, reaching approximately 140 million cumulative miles by March 2023.

The chart 'Global Model 3 cost normalized*' is a horizontal bar chart comparing costs in 2018 versus 2022. The chart uses two horizontal bars to compare cost levels, showing a clear reduction in 2022 compared to 2018. An annotation indicates this represents a '~30% decline' in cost.

Energy Storage deployments (GWh) is a vertical bar chart showing deployments from Q3-2016 through Q1-2023. The Y-axis represents gigawatt-hours (GWh) ranging from 0 to 4. The chart shows a generally upward trend with some volatility. Notable values include a peak around Q3-2020 near 1.5 GWh, a dip in Q4-2020, and a sharp, consistent growth in recent quarters, culminating in the highest value of 3.9 GWh in Q1-2023.

Services & Other gross margin is a vertical bar chart showing margin percentages from Q3'21 through Q1'23. The Y-axis represents percentage values ranging from -4% to 8%. The trend shows significant improvement over the period, starting with a negative margin of approximately -2% in Q3'21, fluctuating near 0% in Q1'22, and then experiencing strong, consistent growth in subsequent quarters, reaching its peak of over 7% in Q1'23.

The 'Vehicle Deliveries' chart is a vertical bar chart showing millions of units delivered from 2Q-2020 to 1Q-2023. The x-axis lists the quarters. Values start at approximately 0.1M in 2Q-2020 and trend steadily upward, reaching a peak of just over 0.4M by 1Q-2023. The overall trend shows consistent growth in quarterly vehicle deliveries over the nearly three-year period.

The 'Operating Cash Flow ($B)' and 'Free Cash Flow ($B)' chart is a grouped vertical bar chart comparing these two financial metrics from 2Q-2020 to 1Q-2023. Blue bars represent Operating Cash Flow and red bars represent Free Cash Flow. Both metrics generally trend upward over time, with Operating Cash Flow reaching a peak of over 5.0B in 3Q-2022. There is significant volatility, particularly in 2Q-2022 where Free Cash Flow dropped to near 0.5B, while Operating Cash Flow was higher.

The 'Net Income ($B)' and 'Adjusted EBITDA ($B)' chart is a grouped vertical bar chart comparing these two metrics from 2Q-2020 to 1Q-2023. Blue bars represent Net Income and red bars represent Adjusted EBITDA. Both metrics show a strong upward trend from 2Q-2020 (near 0) to a peak in 4Q-2022, where Adjusted EBITDA reached roughly 5.5B and Net Income reached nearly 4.0B. 1Q-2023 shows a pullback for both metrics compared to the previous quarter.

Vehicle Deliveries (millions of units) is a bar chart showing trailing 12-month data from 2Q-2020 to 1Q-2023. The x-axis lists the quarters, and the y-axis shows deliveries in millions of units, ranging from 0.0 to 1.6. Values grow steadily from ~0.4 million in 2Q-2020 to ~1.45 million in 1Q-2023, showing a consistent upward trend throughout the period.

Operating Cash Flow vs. Free Cash Flow ($B) is a clustered bar chart comparing the two metrics over a trailing 12-month period from 2Q-2020 to 1Q-2023. The x-axis displays quarters, and the y-axis shows billions of dollars (0 to 20). Operating Cash Flow (blue) starts at ~2.8B and peaks at ~16B in 3Q-2022 before dipping to ~13B in 1Q-2023. Free Cash Flow (maroon) starts at ~1B in 2Q-2020 and reaches a peak of ~9B in 3Q-2022, followed by a decline to ~6B in 1Q-2023. Both metrics show a general upward trend followed by slight cooling in the most recent quarters.

Net Income vs. Adjusted EBITDA ($B) is a clustered bar chart comparing the two metrics over a trailing 12-month period from 2Q-2020 to 1Q-2023. The x-axis lists quarters, and the y-axis shows billions of dollars (0 to 20). Net Income (blue) shows significant growth from near zero in 2Q-2020 to a peak of ~12.5B in 4Q-2022, with a slight decrease to ~11.5B in 1Q-2023. Adjusted EBITDA (maroon) grows steadily from ~4.5B in 2Q-2020 to a peak of ~19B in 4Q-2022, slightly decreasing to ~18.5B in 1Q-2023. Both metrics show a strong, consistent upward trend over the time period.

YoY Revenue Growth: A line chart showing quarterly performance from Q1-2019 to Q1-2023. The vertical axis represents percentage growth from -20% to 90%, and the horizontal axis represents time quarters. The legend includes three series: Tesla (red), Auto Industry (grey), and S&P 500 (blue). Tesla's growth starts high at ~80% in Q1-2019, drops significantly to ~40% in Q3-2019, dips to ~5% in Q1-2020, then rebounds to a peak of ~75% in Q1-2022 before declining to ~40% by Q1-2023. The Auto Industry and S&P 500 remain relatively low, with the Auto Industry dipping as low as -10% around Q3-2020 before recovering to roughly 5% by Q1-2023. The main trend shows Tesla consistently outperforming the Auto Industry and S&P 500 in revenue growth, despite high volatility.

Operating Margin: A line chart showing quarterly performance from Q1-2019 to Q4-2022 (with Tesla continuing to Q1-2023). The vertical axis represents percentage margin from -4% to 18%, and the horizontal axis represents time quarters. The legend includes three series: Tesla (red), Auto Industry (grey), and S&P 500 (blue). Tesla's operating margin starts negative (approx. -1%) in Q1-2019, fluctuates near 0% until Q1-2020, then rises steeply to peak at nearly 17% in Q4-2022 before dropping slightly in Q1-2023. The Auto Industry stays between 2% and 8%. The S&P 500 maintains a steady performance around 10-16%. The main takeaway is Tesla's dramatic improvement in operating efficiency, starting well below the S&P 500 and Auto Industry averages and eventually surpassing both to achieve the highest margins by late 2021.

Market share of Tesla vehicles by region (TTM) line chart. The horizontal axis represents time from Q2 2018 to Q1 2024. The vertical axis represents market share percentage from 0% to 4%. The chart shows three series: US/Canada (blue), Europe (red), and China (green). By Q1 2024, the US/Canada market share is approximately 3.7%, Europe is approximately 2.8%, and China is approximately 2.3%. The main trend shows a consistent upward growth in market share across all three regions over the displayed period, with US/Canada holding the largest share throughout, followed by Europe and China.

The first chart is an area chart titled 'Cumulative miles driven with FSD Beta (billions; as of Apr-21-24)'. The x-axis shows a timeline from Mar-2021 to Mar-2024. The y-axis represents miles in billions, ranging from 0.0 to 1.4. It shows two series: 'FSD Miles' (blue area) and 'FSD V12 Miles' (red area). The data shows steady growth in FSD Miles over time, with a sharp spike and the introduction of FSD V12 Miles reaching nearly 1.4 billion miles by Mar-2024.

The second chart is an area chart titled 'Tesla AI Training Capacity (H100 Equivalent GPUs)'. The x-axis tracks time from Sep-2019 to Mar-2024. The y-axis represents the number of GPUs, ranging from 0 to 40,000. The chart illustrates a gradual increase in GPU capacity from 2019 to 2023, followed by a dramatic, vertical spike in the number of H100 Equivalent GPUs in early 2024, reaching approximately 35,000-40,000.

The 'Non-Automotive gross profit ($M)' chart is a bar chart. The vertical axis represents profit in millions of dollars, ranging from -200 to 600. The horizontal axis represents quarters from Q2 2017 through Q1 2024. The data shows a long period of negative or near-zero gross profit from 2017 to early 2022, followed by a dramatic and consistent upward trend in profitability starting in Q3 2022, peaking at over 500 million in Q4 2023 and remaining high at nearly 500 million in Q1 2024.

The 'Energy Storage deployments (GWh)' chart is a bar chart. The vertical axis represents energy in gigawatt-hours (GWh), ranging from 0 to 4. The horizontal axis represents quarters from Q2 2017 through Q1 2024. The data illustrates a steady, low-level growth from 2017 through 2019, with significant volatility and spikes in 2020 and 2021, followed by a major, rapid increase in deployment volume starting in late 2022 and accelerating through Q1 2024, where deployments reach a record high of approximately 4.1 GWh.

Stacked area chart titled 'Global BEV market share* (12-months trailing)'. The x-axis shows a time period from Q1 2017 to Q1 2024E. The y-axis represents market share percentage from 0% to 12%. The chart displays two data series: 'China' (green) and 'World ex-China' (blue). At the start in Q1 2017, the combined share is roughly 0.5%. By the end in Q1 2024E, the total combined share reaches approximately 11.5%, with 'World ex-China' accounting for about 5% and 'China' accounting for the remaining ~6.5%. The main trend shows a steady, slow growth until around Q3 2020, followed by a significantly steeper upward trajectory in BEV market share for both regions.

Vehicle Deliveries (millions of units) is a vertical bar chart showing quarterly performance from 2Q-2021 to 1Q-2024. The Y-axis represents millions of units, ranging from 0.0 to 0.5. Values are roughly: 2Q-2021 (~0.2), 3Q-2021 (~0.24), 4Q-2021 (~0.31), 1Q-2022 (~0.31), 2Q-2022 (~0.26), 3Q-2022 (~0.34), 4Q-2022 (~0.41), 1Q-2023 (~0.42), 2Q-2023 (~0.47), 3Q-2023 (~0.43), 4Q-2023 (~0.48), 1Q-2024 (~0.39). The trend generally shows steady growth until 1Q-2024, which shows a decline.

Operating Cash Flow ($B) and Free Cash Flow ($B) is a clustered vertical bar chart covering the period from 2Q-2021 to 1Q-2024. The Y-axis ranges from -3 to 6 in billions of dollars. Key approximate values for Operating Cash Flow (blue): 2Q-2021 (~2.1), 3Q-2021 (~3.1), 4Q-2021 (~4.6), 1Q-2022 (~4.0), 2Q-2022 (~2.3), 3Q-2022 (~5.1), 4Q-2022 (~3.3), 1Q-2023 (~2.5), 2Q-2023 (~3.1), 3Q-2023 (~3.3), 4Q-2023 (~4.4), 1Q-2024 (~0.3). Key approximate values for Free Cash Flow (red): 2Q-2021 (~0.6), 3Q-2021 (~1.3), 4Q-2021 (~2.8), 1Q-2022 (~2.2), 2Q-2022 (~0.6), 3Q-2022 (~3.3), 4Q-2022 (~1.4), 1Q-2023 (~0.4), 2Q-2023 (~1.5), 3Q-2023 (~1.3), 4Q-2023 (~2.5), 1Q-2024 (~-2.4). The trend shows fluctuations in cash flow, with a sharp drop in both metrics in 1Q-2024, resulting in negative Free Cash Flow.

Net Income ($B) and Adjusted EBITDA ($B) is a clustered vertical bar chart covering the period from 2Q-2021 to 1Q-2024. The Y-axis ranges from 0 to 8 in billions of dollars. Key approximate values for Net Income (blue): 2Q-2021 (~1.1), 3Q-2021 (~1.6), 4Q-2021 (~2.3), 1Q-2022 (~3.3), 2Q-2022 (~2.3), 3Q-2022 (~3.3), 4Q-2022 (~3.7), 1Q-2023 (~2.5), 2Q-2023 (~2.7), 3Q-2023 (~1.9), 4Q-2023 (~7.9), 1Q-2024 (~1.1). Key approximate values for Adjusted EBITDA (red): 2Q-2021 (~2.5), 3Q-2021 (~3.2), 4Q-2021 (~4.1), 1Q-2022 (~5.0), 2Q-2022 (~3.8), 3Q-2022 (~5.0), 4Q-2022 (~5.4), 1Q-2023 (~4.3), 2Q-2023 (~4.7), 3Q-2023 (~3.8), 4Q-2023 (~4.0), 1Q-2024 (~3.4). Net income peaked significantly in 4Q-2023 before dropping in 1Q-2024, while Adjusted EBITDA has remained more stable, though also trending down from its peak.

The Vehicle Deliveries chart is a bar chart showing the number of vehicles delivered in millions of units from 2Q-2021 to 1Q-2024. The Y-axis represents units in millions (0.0 to 2.0). The chart shows a consistent upward trend in deliveries, starting at ~0.7 million in 2Q-2021, peaking at ~1.8 million in 4Q-2023, with a slight dip to ~1.75 million in 1Q-2024.

The Operating Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow chart is a grouped bar chart displaying two financial metrics in $B from 2Q-2021 to 1Q-2024. The Y-axis range is 0 to 20. The blue bars represent Operating Cash Flow and red bars represent Free Cash Flow. Generally, Operating Cash Flow remained consistently higher than Free Cash Flow. Both metrics peaked around 3Q-2022 (Operating Cash Flow at ~16B and Free Cash Flow at ~9B) and have generally trended downward or fluctuated since, with 1Q-2024 showing Operating Cash Flow at ~11B and Free Cash Flow at ~1.5B.

The Net Income and Adjusted EBITDA chart is a grouped bar chart comparing these two financial metrics in $B from 2Q-2021 to 1Q-2024. The Y-axis ranges from 0 to 20. Blue bars show Net Income and red bars show Adjusted EBITDA. The chart illustrates a growth phase peaking in 2Q-2023 for Adjusted EBITDA (~19B) and 3Q-2023 for Net Income (~15B). In 1Q-2024, Net Income stands at ~13.5B and Adjusted EBITDA at ~15B, showing a decline from the 2023 peaks.

Market share of Tesla vehicles by region (TTM) line chart. The chart plots the percentage market share over time from Q2 2019 to Q1 2025. There are three series: US/Canada (blue line), Europe (red line), and China (green line). The US/Canada line shows growth from approximately 1.2% in Q2 2019 to a peak of around 3.5% around Q4 2023/Q1 2024 before slightly declining to roughly 3.4% by Q1 2025. The Europe line shows a steady increase from nearly 0% in Q2 2019 to approximately 2.5% by Q1 2025. The China line shows growth from near 0% in Q2 2019 to roughly 2.3% by Q1 2025. Overall, the chart indicates a general upward trend in market share for all three regions over the covered period.

Title: Cumulative miles driven with FSD (Supervised) (billions); Chart type: Stacked area chart. Axes: X-axis represents time from Sep-2021 to Mar-2025; Y-axis represents cumulative miles in billions (0.0 to 4.0). Legend: Two series, 'FSD Miles on V12 and Beyond' (red area) and 'FSD Miles on V11 and Before' (blue area). Values: The 'FSD Miles on V11 and Before' series plateaus at approximately 1.0 billion miles starting around March-2024, while the 'FSD Miles on V12 and Beyond' series grows exponentially from March-2024 to reach approximately 3.7 billion total cumulative miles by March-2025. Takeaway: The chart shows a significant shift in cumulative miles driven, where the vast majority of growth from mid-2024 to early 2025 is attributed to FSD V12 and beyond, while the older V11 and before mileage remains constant.

The first chart is a vertical bar chart titled 'Energy and Services and Other gross profit (TTM; $M)'. The y-axis shows profit in millions, ranging from -1,000 to 4,000, and the x-axis displays time by quarter from Q2 2018 to Q1 2025. The chart shows a prolonged period of negative or near-zero gross profit until approximately Q2 2022, followed by a consistent and aggressive upward trend, reaching approximately $3,500 million by Q1 2025.

The second chart is a vertical bar chart titled 'Energy Storage deployments (TTM; GWh)'. The y-axis represents gigawatt-hours from 0 to 40, and the x-axis displays time by quarter from Q2 2018 to Q1 2025. The data shows relatively flat, low deployment levels until roughly Q4 2021, after which there is a steep, exponential growth trajectory, culminating in a record high of approximately 38 GWh by Q1 2025.

The first chart is a column chart titled 'Vehicle Deliveries (millions of units)', covering quarterly periods from 2Q-2022 to 1Q-2025. The y-axis shows units in millions, ranging from 0.0 to 0.5. Values are approximate: 2Q-2022 (~0.25), 3Q-2022 (~0.34), 4Q-2022 (~0.40), 1Q-2023 (~0.42), 2Q-2023 (~0.47), 3Q-2023 (~0.43), 4Q-2023 (~0.48), 1Q-2024 (~0.38), 2Q-2024 (~0.44), 3Q-2024 (~0.46), 4Q-2024 (~0.49), and 1Q-2025 (~0.36). The trend shows generally upward growth interrupted by periodic dips, peaking at 4Q-2024 before a decline in 1Q-2025.

The second chart is a clustered column chart comparing 'Operating Cash Flow ($B)' (blue) and 'Free Cash Flow ($B)' (red) from 2Q-2022 to 1Q-2025. The y-axis represents values in billions, ranging from -3 to 7. Key approximate values include: Operating Cash Flow peaks at 3Q-2024 (~6.3B) and 3Q-2022 (~5.1B), while Free Cash Flow shows high volatility with a significant negative dip in 1Q-2024 (~ -2.5B). The trend shows both metrics generally tracking together, though with significant fluctuations and a stark negative value for Free Cash Flow in 1Q-2024.

The third chart is a clustered column chart comparing 'Net Income ($B)' (blue) and 'Adjusted EBITDA ($B)' (red) from 2Q-2022 to 1Q-2025. The y-axis ranges from 0 to 8. Net Income exhibits notable spikes, particularly in 4Q-2023 (~7.9B), while Adjusted EBITDA shows more consistent levels, generally ranging between ~3.5B and ~5.5B. Most quarters show Adjusted EBITDA being higher than Net Income, with the exception of 4Q-2023 where Net Income is significantly higher.

Vehicle Deliveries (millions of units) is a bar chart showing quarterly data from 2Q-2022 to 1Q-2025. The y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 2.0. Deliveries generally trended upward from ~1.1 million in 2Q-2022 to a peak of ~1.8 million in 4Q-2023, after which they have fluctuated slightly but remained between ~1.7 and 1.8 million.

Operating Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow is a grouped bar chart displaying two financial metrics in billions of dollars ($B) across quarters from 2Q-2022 to 1Q-2025. Operating Cash Flow (blue bars) started at ~14B and fluctuated, generally trending lower to ~11B in 1Q-2024 before rising again to ~17B in 1Q-2025. Free Cash Flow (red bars) shows more significant volatility, starting at ~7B, peaking near 9B in 3Q-2022, dipping to ~1.5B in 1Q-2024, and rising to ~7B in 1Q-2025.

Net Income and Adjusted EBITDA is a grouped bar chart showing two financial metrics in billions of dollars ($B) from 2Q-2022 to 1Q-2025. Net Income (blue bars) ranged from a low of ~6B in 1Q-2025 to a peak of ~15B in 4Q-2023. Adjusted EBITDA (red bars) is consistently higher than Net Income, ranging from ~15B to ~19B through most of the period, before trending down to ~15B in 1Q-2025.

The chart, titled 'Market share of Tesla vehicles by region (TTM)', is a line graph displaying the market share percentage over time from Q2 2017 to Q2 2023. The graph features three lines representing different regions: US/Canada (blue), Europe (red), and China (green). The Y-axis represents percentage share (0% to 4%) and the X-axis represents quarterly time periods. As of Q2 2023, the US/Canada region reaches approximately 4%, Europe reaches approximately 2.8%, and China reaches approximately 2.2%. The main trend shows a consistent upward trajectory in market share for all three regions, particularly accelerating since 2021.

The 'Cumulative miles driven with FSD Beta (millions)' chart is a line graph covering the period from March 2021 to June 2023. The x-axis plots months from Mar-21 to Jun-23, and the y-axis plots cumulative miles in millions from 0 to 350. The graph shows a steady, accelerating upward trend in FSD Beta usage, starting at near zero and rising to approximately 300+ million miles by June 2023.

The 'Internal projection of Dojo compute power' chart is a line graph covering the period from January 2023 to October 2024. The y-axis represents 'In Units Of A100 GPUs' from 0 to 400,000, and the x-axis represents the date. The blue line depicts the growth of Tesla's internal compute power, which remains relatively flat until mid-2023 before curving sharply upward, projected to reach 100 Exa-Flops of compute power by October 2024. The chart includes annotations for 'Start of Dojo Production' around mid-2023 and 'Top 5 in the Entire World Projected' around early 2024.

The 'Energy Storage deployments (GWh)' chart is a bar chart showing quarterly deployment numbers from Q4 2016 through Q2 2023. The vertical axis represents GWh, ranging from 0 to 4. The bars generally show an upward trend over time, with notable spikes in Q1 2021 (approx. 1.5 GWh), Q1 2023 (nearly 4 GWh), and Q2 2023 (approx. 3.7 GWh). The overall trend indicates significant growth in energy storage deployments, especially in the most recent periods.

The 'Services & Other gross margin' chart is a bar chart showing quarterly gross margin percentages from Q4 2016 through Q2 2023. The vertical axis represents percentages, ranging from -50% to 10%. The bars represent negative margins for most of the historical period, bottoming out around Q1/Q2 2018 (near -45%). There is a clear upward trend leading to positive margins starting in Q3 2022, with the most recent data points for Q1 and Q2 2023 showing consistent positive margins around 7-8%.

The 'Vehicle Deliveries' chart is a vertical bar chart covering the period from 3Q-2020 to 2Q-2023. The vertical axis represents units in millions, ranging from 0.0 to 0.5. The chart shows a generally consistent upward trend in vehicle deliveries, growing from ~0.14 million units in 3Q-2020 to a peak of ~0.47 million units in 2Q-2023.

The 'Operating Cash Flow ($B)' and 'Free Cash Flow ($B)' chart is a grouped vertical bar chart covering 3Q-2020 to 2Q-2023. The vertical axis represents dollars in billions, ranging from 0 to 6. Operating Cash Flow (blue) and Free Cash Flow (red) show significant quarterly fluctuation but overall growth; notably, Operating Cash Flow hit a peak of over 5 billion in 3Q-2022, while Free Cash Flow reached its highest point of roughly 3.3 billion in the same quarter.

The 'Net Income ($B)' and 'Adjusted EBITDA ($B)' chart is a grouped vertical bar chart covering 3Q-2020 to 2Q-2023. The vertical axis represents dollars in billions, ranging from 0 to 6. The data shows a strong upward trajectory for both metrics: Adjusted EBITDA (red) grew from under 2 billion in 3Q-2020 to a peak of over 5 billion in 4Q-2022, while Net Income (blue) grew from nearly 0 to a peak of nearly 4 billion in 4Q-2022, showing a generally positive correlation between the two metrics.

The first chart is a bar chart titled 'Vehicle Deliveries (millions of units)'. It covers the time period from 3Q-2020 to 2Q-2023. The vertical axis represents millions of units, ranging from 0.0 to 1.8. Deliveries show a consistent upward trend over the period, growing from approximately 0.4 million in 3Q-2020 to approximately 1.6-1.7 million in 2Q-2023.

The second chart is a grouped bar chart with two series: 'Operating Cash Flow ($B)' (blue) and 'Free Cash Flow ($B)' (red). It covers the period from 3Q-2020 to 2Q-2023. The vertical axis represents billions of dollars, ranging from 0 to 20. Both metrics generally trended upward from 3Q-2020 to 3Q-2022, peaking in 3Q-2022, before dipping and then stabilizing/slightly recovering in 2023.

The third chart is a grouped bar chart with two series: 'Net Income ($B)' (blue) and 'Adjusted EBITDA ($B)' (red). It covers the period from 3Q-2020 to 2Q-2023. The vertical axis represents billions of dollars, ranging from 0 to 20. Both metrics show a strong, consistent growth trend from 2020 through 2022, reaching peaks around 4Q-2022, followed by a slight plateau or minor decline in the first half of 2023.

The 'YoY Revenue Growth' chart is a line chart covering the period from Q2-2019 to Q1-2023. It tracks the year-over-year revenue growth percentages for three entities: Tesla (red line), Auto Industry (grey line), and S&P 500 (blue line). Tesla's growth started high at over 80% in Q2-2019, dropped significantly to around 15% by Q4-2019, then climbed to over 70% in Q1-2022 before declining to around 40% by Q1-2023. The Auto Industry fluctuated mostly between -10% and 15%, while the S&P 500 stayed relatively stable, generally fluctuating between 0% and 15%. Tesla experienced significant volatility compared to the other two indices.

The 'Operating Margin' chart is a line chart covering the period from Q2-2019 to Q2-2023. It tracks the operating margin percentages for three entities: Tesla (red line), Auto Industry (grey line), and S&P 500 (blue line). Tesla's margin began near 0% in Q2-2019 and trended steadily upward, reaching a peak of nearly 17% in Q4-2022 before dipping to just under 14% in Q2-2023. The Auto Industry's margin hovered between 2% and 8% throughout the period. The S&P 500's margin remained relatively consistent, oscillating between 10% and 16%, peaking around Q1-2022. The main takeaway is Tesla's significant improvement in operating margins, which surpassed both the Auto Industry and the S&P 500 averages by 2021-2022.

The chart is a line graph titled 'Market share of Tesla vehicles by region (TTM)'. The vertical axis represents a percentage scale from 0% to 4%, and the horizontal axis represents time from Q3 2018 to Q2 2024. The legend shows three lines: 'US/Canada' (blue), 'Europe' (red), and 'China' (green). By Q2 2024, the US/Canada market share is approximately 3.5%, Europe is approximately 2.6%, and China is approximately 2.2%. The main trend shows that Tesla's market share in all three regions has experienced growth since 2018, with the US/Canada region consistently maintaining the highest share, though growth has leveled off or slightly declined since Q3/Q4 2023.

The 'Cumulative miles driven with FSD (Supervised)' chart is an area chart covering the period from June 2021 to June 2024. The y-axis represents billions of miles, ranging from 0.0 to 1.6. The series are 'FSD V12 Miles' (red) and 'FSD Miles' (blue). The data shows a relatively slow, steady increase until around June 2023, followed by a sharper, accelerating upward trend. By June 2024, total cumulative miles reach approximately 1.5 billion, with the FSD V12 component contributing significantly to the recent growth.

The 'Tesla AI training capacity ramp through end of year (H100 equivalent GPUs)' chart is a step chart covering the period from June 2021 to December 2024. The y-axis represents capacity in units ranging from 0 to 90,000. The series are 'Existing Capacity' (solid line) and 'Future Planned Capacity' (dotted line). The data shows incremental, step-like growth in capacity over time, with a significant jump occurring between March 2024 and June 2024. The capacity hits a plateau of roughly 35,000 units around mid-2024, with 'Future Planned Capacity' showing a sharp, rapid projected increase to approximately 90,000 units by December 2024.

The 'Non-Automotive gross profit ($M)' chart is a vertical bar chart. The x-axis represents time periods by quarter, starting from Q3 2017 to Q2 2024. The y-axis shows profit in millions of dollars, ranging from -1,000 to 1,000. For most of the early period up to Q1 2022, the bars show negative or near-zero profit, with dips around Q1 2019 and Q1 2021. Starting in Q2 2022, profit turns positive and shows a consistent upward trend, culminating in a significant peak of approximately $900 million in Q2 2024.

The 'Energy Storage deployments (GWh)' chart is a vertical bar chart. The x-axis represents time periods by quarter from Q3 2017 to Q2 2024. The y-axis represents gigawatt-hours (GWh) ranging from 0 to 10. The chart shows relatively low, steady deployment from 2017 to 2020. Growth begins to accelerate noticeably from 2021 onwards. There is a sharp spike in the final bar for Q2 2024, reaching a value slightly below 10 GWh (approximately 9.4 GWh as noted in the text).

The chart is a stacked area chart titled 'Global BEV market share* (12-months trailing)'. The X-axis represents time from Q1 2017 to Q2 2024E, and the Y-axis represents percentage market share from 0% to 12%. The chart includes two series: 'China' (represented by the green area on top) and 'World ex-China' (represented by the blue area at the bottom). In Q1 2017, the total market share was near 0%. By Q2 2024E, the total market share reached approximately 12%, with the 'World ex-China' portion contributing roughly 5% and the 'China' portion contributing the remaining ~7%. The main trend shows a consistent and accelerating growth in global BEV market share over the 7-year period, with China consistently accounting for a larger portion of this growth compared to the rest of the world.

The 'Vehicle Deliveries' chart is a vertical bar chart representing millions of units delivered from 3Q-2021 to 2Q-2024. The Y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 0.5.
